newsitem.title: USA: Nu Skin sees Japan strong, S. Korea weak.
newsitem.headline: Nu Skin sees Japan strong, S. Korea weak.

text.p: Nu Skin Asia Pacific Inc said Wednesday it expects strong trends to continue in Japan, where it makes more than half of its revenues, but sees weakness in South Korea.

Nu Skin posted second quarter profits of $0.27 a share after a pretax distributor stock expense of $4,477,000, compared with $0.25 last year. Sales rose 40.7 percent to $230.0 million, with a 58.8 percent jump in Japan to $144.7 million.

Nu Skin said it "anticipates continued strong results overall, with particular strength in Japan," although it noted that it has historically experienced modest growth in the third quarter due primarily to the vacation season.
In the third quarter, it said it plans to introduce an aloe vera drink developed specifically for the Japanese market and Interior Design Sports Nutrition products in Taiwan.

The growth in Japan reflects a new distributor stock option program and a strong reception for new products including fiber dietary supplement FibreNet and the four-product Multi-Hydroxy Acid skin care system. The new products accounted for more than five percent of second quarter revenue in Japan.

South Korean sales fell sharply, down 28.6 percent to $23.0 million, and the company expects further softening. It said the shortfall was aggravated by slowing economic growth, "buy Korean" campaigns and bad publicity.

Nu Skin said it plans product promotions and public relations efforts in the South Korean market, which it believes will be "very receptive" to the new Interior Design products when they debut later this year.
